title: What do you think of the look and style of this game?
author: Gambo7592
selftext:
I'm experimenting with some "Risograph" style games and wanted some feedback, working on colorblind friendly options is the main issue with this. I can't tell if I like it or not lmao 

Free to play, No Ads: [https://tbone94.github.io/Riso-Runner/](https://tbone94.github.io/Riso-Runner/) 

any feedback is welcome

comments.author: thelonelyemptiness
comments.body:
Hi. This look cool!  
I think maybe a little bit of screen shaking to simulate the running and some wind visual effects. Maybe some areas with more obstacles with a bit of parkour would be interesting and in the future maybe a roguelike game mode (?), I dont know how it could be implemented, maybe with some enemies or random obstacles.  
Nice game concept

comments.author: NikopikVR
comments.body: Could be a cool VR exercize game

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body: Painfully bright and blurry. Make it stop.

comments.author: TechgeekOne
comments.body: The screen space noise could use some tuning or be swapped out for a more standard dither pattern. As-is it's really harsh on the eyes to me.

replies.author: Gambo7592
replies.body:
Yeah that's my worry. The RIsograph Print look kinda cool but also creates a lot of visual noise and makes it look more pixelated. I'll try working with other patterns but im not sold on this "style" working in a 1st person pov/3D world. Works better on flat 2d worlds   
Thanks for advice and feedback!

replies.author: Gambo7592
replies.body: phew, ok good I was worried it wasn't working

comments.author: NotSoSuperShay
comments.body:
Ramblings from work break:  
  
I like it a lot! I like the idea of the Risograph but I think there is too much white. Right now it looks like the ink drums all need more ink. It's okay to have a few off to slightly change the visual but it comes off as grainy. 

The game play starts off a little slow I think even for a beginner. I think right around teh 5k part it starts to get interesting. The most interesting part was the transition phase. Moving out of desert into snow and still seeing one or two tumbleweeds or vice versa, being on an icy road with a tumbleweed coming.  

Tumbleweed needs some adjustments you don't really have to account for it until well after 5k. Which could mean, "I have been running and ignoring this thing for so long, why do I need to pay attention now?"   
You have told the runner this is nearly a moot point, now all of sudden it matters. 

Timer for slide could be added, because then it gives one more timer for the user to experience and possible lose at. I cant hold W down and continue to fly, so why S lets me continue to slide. 

Sent a DM! Keep it up!
